Positivism is a narrower doctrine that holds knowledge must rest on empirically verifiable observation and rejects metaphysics and non-testable claims. Naturalism is broader: it holds that the natural world and scientific methods are the proper basis for understanding everything, including human affairs, without appeal to the supernatural or to a separate "first philosophy." Positivism is therefore best seen as one strict version of the naturalist outlook, and naturalism can tolerate theoretical entities and philosophy that positivism would reject.
